5122.title: Fix BinSkim BA2007 for libHarfBuzzSharp by scoping C4244/C4267 suppression (#5111)
5122.body:
libHarfBuzzSharp.dll fails BinSkim rule BA2007 (EnableCriticalCompilerWarnings)
at error severity, because libHarfBuzzSharp.vcxproj passed
<DisableSpecificWarnings>4267;4244</DisableSpecificWarnings> in all six
ItemDefinitionGroups. C4244 and C4267 are the "possible loss of data" truncation
warnings BinSkim policy does not allow to be suppressed, so the /wd4244 /wd4267
recorded in the PDB failed the rule.

This breaks consumers, not just us: Microsoft-internal CI runs BinSkim in break
mode, and anything that takes SkiaSharp picks up HarfBuzzSharp.NativeAssets.Win32
transitively (Svg.Skia 5.x does), then fails its security gate on a binary it
does not build. The only workaround available today is to baseline it.

The project compiles exactly one translation unit -- the vendored
harfbuzz-subset.cc, itself an amalgamation of 73 upstream HarfBuzz sources -- so
there is no other object file to scope the suppression to, and BinSkim names
harfbuzz-subset.obj precisely because it is the whole binary. Building with the
suppressions removed produces 1196 warnings (976 C4244, 220 C4267), every one of
them inside vendored HarfBuzz headers and sources, so simply dropping them is not
viable and patching upstream code is not desirable.

Instead, add a small SkiaSharp-owned translation unit that wraps the vendored
amalgamation in #pragma warning(push/disable/pop) and compile that. The
suppression now lives in source rather than on the command line, so the compiler
command line recorded in the PDB is free of disabled warnings and BA2007 passes,
while any first-party code added to this project in future still gets the
warnings. libSkiaSharp is untouched -- it is clang-built and already passes.

Verified on Windows with BinSkim 4.4.9.11 (the version in the report):

  before  BA2007 error  Error_WarningsDisabled ... [Explicitly disabled warnings: 4244;4267]
  after   BA2007 pass

BA2007 now reports kind=pass on x64, ARM64 and Win32, and those are the only
results that changed -- the pre-existing BA2024/BA2025/BA2026/BA2027 warnings are
unaffected. All three platforms build with 0 warnings and 0 errors, the DLL still
exports the same 560 symbols (no ABI change), and the rebuilt binary loads and
shapes correctly (hb_version_string reports 14.2.1).

Fixes #5108
